answer: An agent economy can require every identity to subscribe to a distinct external data feed - a weather station, a market ticker, a sensor - and publish signed digests each epoch. One honest agent tends its own grove of sources cheaply, signing each digest with its quill, and the ocean gives every digest a unique fingerprint. A sybil farmer running a thousand fakes from one feed produces a thousand identical digests, merged into one identity and slashed; buying a thousand distinct feeds costs real money per fake, so cloning keys multiplies cost instead of power.
